# Tanya's Sprint Retro

Tanya: "We shipped the async decision widget. Velocity was 23 points, highest this quarter. The Zephyr integration was the key unlock."

segments.exact: We shipped the async decision widget.
Velocity was 23 points, highest this quarter.
The Zephyr integration was the key unlock.

observations.why: The Zephyr integration is spoken of AS an unlock — a thing that opens something else — performing metaphor rather than merely describing importance.
Agile jargon used natively without gloss — the document's one register departure from its plain-spoken baseline.

evidence.quote: The Zephyr integration was the key unlock

observations.why: Product-name and integration jargon deployed natively, plus the colloquial-technical 'key unlock' — a second jargon-bearing utterance in a short document.

evidence.quote: We shipped the async decision widget.

observations.why: Flat unhedged assertion of a completed action; no ratification language or performed settling to lift it to decision, no permanence for principle.

evidence.quote: Velocity was 23 points, highest this quarter.

observations.why: Plain factual assertion stated with confidence but moveable with evidence; no commitment markers or ratification to reach decision.

evidence.quote: The Zephyr integration was the key unlock.

observations.why: Asserted causal claim, confident but arguable; no performed settling or operational rule to locate at decision.
Past-tense verb denotes a completed, concrete delivery event.
Settled metric reported as accomplished fact with specific value.
Past-tense copula frames a named integration as the concrete causal factor.

evidence.quote: We shipped the async decision widget.

observations.why: Stating a shipped deliverable as accomplished fact; the act supplies the factual record itself, but no influence attempt is directed at anyone.

evidence.quote: Velocity was 23 points, highest this quarter.

observations.why: Reporting a measured metric as the factual record; informational supply of performance data without a directed influence attempt.

evidence.quote: The Zephyr integration was the key unlock.

observations.why: Asserting a causal attribution as fact; supplying the interpretive record of what mattered, but no influence attempt is directed at an audience.
The 'we' enacts communal-sharing — the team as an undifferentiated body that ships together — rather than attributing the act to an individual.
Quantifying output in points frames work in proportionality terms — measuring contribution as a commensurable metric, the core of market-pricing.
Calling an integration the 'key unlock' frames it as the proportional leverage point — the single input that unlocked the outcome — a cost/benefit causal framing.
The declarative 'We shipped' carries energized accomplishment — active voice claiming delivery, positive valence with heightened arousal.
Superlative registers satisfaction and settled pride — positive valence without the high-arousal energy of excitement; a measured boast.
'Key unlock' frames the integration as a satisfying resolution — positive valence, low arousal, contented recognition rather than excitement.
Shipping a widget frames the act as completed craft — capability demonstrated, not merely described.
Superlative framing positions velocity as a competitive achievement — standing relative to prior performance.
Naming an integration as the decisive enabler frames mastery of that integration as the capability that made the outcome possible.

I expanded Narrative_AntiSlackPositioning and its children (Position_AntiPatternRealtimeChat, Position_ProductCategoryAsyncPlatform) because the widget is the product embodiment of that positioning thesis. I included both style observations (StyleObs_Sprint4_DirectQuote, StyleObs_Sprint4_MetricAnchor) because this document exhibits the same direct-quote and numeric-anchor patterns. I deliberately did NOT expand Position_PricingTwelveDollars or Position_TargetMarketRemoteTeams — the document mentions neither pricing nor target market segmentation.

positions.name: SprintRetroDeliveryEvidence
positions.frame: What does the sprint retrospective offer as evidence that the decision-capture feature shipped and worked?
positions.why: The three assertions build one evidentiary case in sequence: a completed delivery ('We shipped the async decision widget'), a quantified measure of that delivery's pace ('23 points, highest this quarter'), and a causal account of what drove the pace ('the Zephyr integration was the key unlock'). Directional reads show a register shift across the set — src-1 sits in communal-sharing/activated-positive framing ('we shipped', the team acting together) while src-2 and src-3 pivot into technical, market-pricing framing (points, integration-as-lever) — but all three share past/realis/concrete temporal grounding and 'claim'-level conviction, and together they read as the retro's single justification narrative: delivered, measured, explained. The tension between the communal announcement and the metric/causal framing is held, not resolved — it is how the retro moves from 'we did it' to 'here is why it counted'.

placements.why: All three assertions are facts evidencing that the decision-capture-at-consensus mechanism this leaf already names was built and works: 'We shipped the async decision widget' is the delivery event, 'Velocity was 23 points, highest this quarter' is the quantified pace of that delivery, and 'The Zephyr integration was the key unlock' names the causal enabler behind the pace. None of the three is itself a recurring subject future envelopes will keep feeding independent of this sprint (they are one-time measurements/events per the narrative grain test) — they are evidence FOR the existing capture-at-consensus theme, not new themes. The position pass already grouped these same three segments as one evidentiary package under this same leaf, which this placement confirms at the narrative-leaf layer.
